1,0,1: Luke Badiali closed the programme with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley on financial and commercial modelling. Using utilisation, day rates and bid costs we found each tender win costs around 55 consultant days of bid effort. We built three revenue scenarios for the shift from tenders to pre-tender shaping and agreed pricing and margin targets.
5,1,1: Programme complete; quarterly check-ins to track tender share and bid days per win.
5,2,1: Kate to prepare a quarterly scorecard covering tender share, pre-tender conversations and bid days per win.
2,1,1: Andrew's data showed 46 bids at about 12 days each against 10 wins, so roughly 55 bid days per win. Kate said this has never been costed before.
2,2,1: Average utilisation is 64 percent and the blended day rate is 1,050 pounds. Luke noted that freeing bid days could lift utilisation if pre-tender work converts.
2,3,1: Andrew wanted a downside case if pre-tender shaping takes longer than expected to show results.
3,3,1: Track bid days per win as the core acquisition cost metric, targeting a reduction from 55 to 30 days within 12 months.
3,1,1: Raise the blended day rate from 1,050 to 1,150 pounds for regulated-sector work from April.
3,2,1: Set a minimum programme margin of 35 percent, with subcontract work held to the 25 percent floor.
3,7,1: Use three scenarios for next year: downside 5.2m, base 5.9m and upside 6.6m, with base assuming 50 percent of revenue from tenders.
4,1,0: Present the three revenue scenarios to the board
